summary: Pakistan’s conservation commitments expand protected areas from 12% to 15% of national land by 2023 and manage at least 1.5 million ha of snow-leopard habitat; flood measures cover 2.47 million ha protected from inundation, 779,250 ha from erosion and 154,180 ha reclaimed. Restoration leads the mixed agenda: by 2030, restore 30% of degraded forest, 5% of degraded cropland, 6% of degraded grassland and 10% of degraded wetlands. Major programmes include 1.2 million ha of forest restoration by 2023, 1 million ha of mass afforestation, 145,300 ha under sustainable forest management and 350,000 ha in the Indus delta. The 1.2-million-ha programme equals an area equal to about 62% of ESA’s 2022 forest cover. Other mixed pledges target 16,552 ha of new mangrove plantations, a 6.5% forest share and 148.76 MtCO2e of sequestration by 2030, alongside six recharge sites.
